cs.t: I use a Fnatic MiniStreak TKL (no numpad). I never used numpads much, and I like to be able to keep my mouse hand in closer. Switches are Cherry MX Browns. Custom keycaps, though that's only for appearance (pudding caps to diffuse the RGB), doesn't alter performance. A gamer keyboard very much leaning into the "esports" theme, but excellent for typing on too. Price was reasonable as mechanical keyboards go. Had it for quite a while now, very happy with it. Don't think they sell this particular keyboard anymore, this is probably the nearest to it in their current range:  https://fnatic.com/products/mini-streak-rgb-tenkeyless-silen...
cs.th: Ask HN: Which computer keyboard do you use?

cs.t: I use a Fnatic MiniStreak mechanical keyboard. Somewhat cheaper than the top end brands, but still very good. There is software if you want to configure LEDs and macros and such (it's gamer gear, so it's bedecked in coloured lights), but you don't have to install it. Mind you, that's true of most Logitech gear too - it'll work fine with basic Windows drivers, you don't have to install that G Hub Pro whatever-it-is stuff. Some of their mice also have on-board memory for settings - you can configure them once using the software, write the config to the mouse, then not bother with the software again.
cs.th: Ask HN: What's your favorite software-free keyboard and mouse?
